scriptWithTimestamps:
So you have this data. Now what?

First, compare how the three engines answer the same query. You might find that Google AI Mode cites your competitor's blog post, Perplexity pulls from a completely different source, and ChatGPT doesn't mention either of you. That tells you exactly where your gaps are and where the opportunities lie.

Second, look at the sources. Which domains keep showing up across all three engines? Those are the authoritative sources for your topic. If you're not among them, analyze why. that's your content brief right there. Figure out what those pages are doing differently, whether it's structure, depth, citations, or format, and adapt.

Third, track changes over time. AI answers are volatile. Research shows that forty to sixty percent of citations change month to month. If you're only checking once, you're only seeing a snapshot. Scheduled runs give you the full picture.

And finally, use the regional data. A query might return completely different AI answers in the US versus Germany, versus Japan. If you're running international campaigns, this is how you catch localization issues before they hurt your traffic.
